headline: A quiet Sunday in Washington
summary: Roosevelt is in Washington; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Waiting on the Nashville
summary: Roosevelt talks with Representatives Cannon and Mondell, greets the sailors of the Sylph and Mayflower, lunches with John W. Foster, and leaves that night for Oyster Bay. The Panama rising planned for this day is held back until U.S. warships take station; the Nashville reaches Colon by 5:30.

events.detail: Talks with Joe Cannon and Frank Mondell
Welcomes sailors from the Mayflower and Sylph
Panama revolt delayed until the Nashville, Boston and Dixie are in place; Nashville anchors at Colon
Leaves at night for Oyster Bay

headline: Panama declares independence
summary: Roosevelt votes at Oyster Bay on Election Day, sees Jacob Riis, and heads back to Washington that evening. In Panama City, Colombian troops are bought off with $50 apiece in gold, railroad workers and firemen seize the city, U.S. ships keep Colombian forces from landing, and Panama proclaims independence with Dr. Amador as president.

events.detail: Casts his ballot at Oyster Bay
Revolution in Panama City: General Huertas's troops are paid off, rebels take the city, independence proclaimed
American warships offshore block Colombian landings
Letters to Seth Low, Ted and Kermit

letters.topic: Regrets Low's loss in the mayoral race
Ted misses home; Alice is well
About to dictate a Panama message; Groton's football win

uncertain: The record says U.S. recognition came within a day and a half, but its own entry for November 6 dates the recognition to that day.

headline: Marines ashore at Colon
summary: American Marines come ashore at Colon. Roosevelt writes Nicholas Murray Butler about the elections, including a lengthy rundown of his reading since 1900, and writes Hanna on the canal and Gilder on the coal strike.

events.detail: Letters to Butler, Hanna and Gilder
His three-year reading list goes to Butler

letters.topic: Election results and what he has been reading
The canal
The coal strike

references.title: Theodore Roosevelt and His Time, by Joseph Bucklin Bishop

headline: War council on the Panama rising
summary: Roosevelt meets Hay, Moody, Loomis and Admirals Taylor and Walker on events in Panama, sees the immigration commissioners, and has Senator and Mrs. George Turner overnight. He writes General Francis Greene on the elections and Lyman Abbott about Hanna's place in the presidential picture.

events.detail: Panama crisis talks with Hay, Moody, Loomis and Admirals Walker and Taylor
Dines with the Hays, Moody, Crane and Admiral Walker
Senator and Mrs. George Turner stay the night

letters.topic: The elections
Hanna and the presidency

references.title: Theodore Roosevelt and His Time, by Joseph Bucklin Bishop

headline: America recognizes the Republic of Panama
summary: The United States recognizes Panama, and the Cabinet agrees to open canal treaty talks with the new republic at once. Roosevelt sees Congressmen Grosvenor and Hepburn, dines with Governor Franklin Murphy, and insists to Albert Shaw there was no conspiracy with the rebels.

events.detail: U.S. recognition of the Republic of Panama
Cabinet decides to seek a canal treaty with Panama immediately
Letters to Guild, Admiral Walker, Albert Shaw, Hay and a general testimonial

letters.topic: Thanks
Not described
Not described
Denies any U.S. plot behind the revolt
Panama

headline: Senate leaders and the Cuba treaty
summary: On a crowded day Roosevelt meets Senators Spooner, Aldrich, Cullom, Allison, Hale and Orville Platt about changes to the Cuban treaty, lunches with John Sleicher, and dines with General Francis Greene. He writes Hay on Congress's role in foreign affairs.

events.detail: Cuban treaty amendments with six senators
Lunch with John Sleicher; dinner with Francis Greene
Letters to Hay, Brokmeyer and John Bassett Moore

letters.topic: How far Congress's power reaches in foreign affairs
Not described
Hay drew on Moore's opinions

headline: Late-night talks with Root and Aldrich
summary: Roosevelt meets Elihu Root at nine about Panama and Senator Aldrich at ten about finance.

headline: Congress meets in special session
summary: Congress gathers in extra session to act on Cuban reciprocity. Roosevelt discusses the Republican National Committee chairmanship with Hanna, dines with Lodge, and spends the evening with a roomful of party leaders over his Cuba message. He presses for Spring-Rice's posting to Washington.

events.detail: Special session of Congress opens on Cuban reciprocity
With Hanna on who should chair the national committee
Evening session on the Cuba message with Moody and congressional leaders
To Spring-Rice on a posting to the British embassy

letters.topic: Hopes he will be assigned to the Washington embassy

headline: Cuba message goes to Congress; Booker T. Washington calls
summary: Roosevelt sends Congress his special message on Cuban reciprocity after a Cabinet session on Panama. He meets a joint committee including Hanna, Lodge and Cannon at 10:30, lunches with Baroness von Sternberg, sees Booker T. Washington at 2:30, and dines with House leaders.

events.detail: Special message on Cuban reciprocity sent to Congress
Dinner with Payne, Dalzell, Hemenway and Tawney

works.title: Special message to Congress on Cuban reciprocity

headline: Dinner with Root
summary: Roosevelt dines with Secretary Root.

headline: "We did not know"
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts with Senator Beveridge and holds an evening dinner conference on Panama with Hay, Wilson and a group of senators. He assures Jacob Schurman and Lawrence Abbott that he and Hay had no advance knowledge of the Panama revolution.

events.detail: Panama dinner with Hay, Wilson and Senators Allison, Platt, Spooner, Hanna, Fairbanks and Hale
Letters to Schurman and Lawrence Abbott

Same assurance about Panama

headline: Receiving Panama's minister
summary: At 9:30 Roosevelt receives Philippe Bunau-Varilla as Panama's minister. After Cabinet and talks with Senators Fairbanks, Hoar, Allison and McComas, he lunches with Knox and dines with Lodge and Hay. To James Wilson he recalls urging McKinley in 1898 to treat Spanish torpedo boats' sailing as an act of war.

events.detail: Receives Bunau-Varilla as minister of Panama
With Senators McComas, Hoar, Fairbanks and Allison
Lunches with Knox, then dines with Hay and Lodge
To James Wilson recalling his advice before the Spanish war

letters.topic: What he told McKinley's Cabinet before war with Spain

tr_quotes.text: at that time I urged that Spain should be notified that we would treat the sailing of Spanish armed vessels and torpedo boats as an act of war.

headline: A scramble up Rock Creek
summary: After meeting Hanna and Puerto Rican delegates, Roosevelt leads Ethel, Archie, Quentin and three Garfield boys on a scramble through Rock Creek Park. That evening he dines with members of the Ellis Island investigating commission.

events.detail: With Hanna and delegates from Puerto Rico
Rock Creek Park scramble with his children and three Garfield sons
Dinner for the Ellis Island commission

headline: Acting as "vice-mother"
summary: Roosevelt has dinner with Lodge and his sister Bamie and her husband. With Edith away nine days, he tells Kermit he spends 45 minutes every evening reading aloud to the two little boys, from Algonquin legends and Scott to Macaulay, Jim Bludso and the Bible. Ted has broken his nose at football.

events.detail: Dinner with the Cowleses and Lodge
Nightly reading to Archie and Quentin while Edith is away

letters.topic: Edith's absence and bedtime reading
His broken nose

headline: Speech on Lincoln at New York Avenue church
summary: At Congressman Hitt's request, the House receives the Panama documents. Roosevelt sees Beveridge, Fairbanks, Moody, Cortelyou, Cannon and Governor Durbin, lunches with Hughitt, Hendricks and Low, and at 7:45 gives an address on Lincoln at New York Avenue Presbyterian Church. He sends Harvard's football team a rousing letter.

events.detail: Panama documents sent to the House on Hitt's request
Callers and conferences with Fairbanks, Beveridge, Cannon, Cortelyou, Moody and Governor Durbin
Lunch guests Low, Hendricks and Marvin Hughitt
Encouragement to Harvard's football team via Cranston

letters.topic: A pep talk for the Harvard eleven

headline: Senators to dinner as the treaty takes shape
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt lunches with Governor Durbin, Justice Harlan and others while Bunau-Varilla and Hay draft a canal treaty. He dines with Lodge, Root, Knox and a table of senators, and writes on labor unions and the canal.

events.detail: Lunch with Durbin, Harlan, Sheffield and Fitzgerald
Hay and Bunau-Varilla work on a canal treaty
Dinner with Lodge, Root, Knox and Senators Penrose, Frye, Kean, Proctor, Quay and Foraker
Letters to Edwin Packard and William McAdoo

The canal

headline: Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty signed
summary: At 6:40 in the evening John Hay and Philippe Bunau-Varilla sign the canal treaty between the United States and Panama, on the same $10 million terms Colombia had refused. Earlier Roosevelt sees Simon Wolf and lunches with Moody, Ream and Wayne MacVeagh.

events.detail: Lunch with MacVeagh, Moody and Ream
Hay and Bunau-Varilla sign the Panama canal treaty

headline: Quentin's birthday cake in the nursery
summary: Quentin turns six, nursing a cold; his birthday cake is brought up to the nursery, where Edith, Aunt Emily, Ethel, Archie, his father, Mame and Georgette join him. The House passes the Cuban reciprocity bill, Roosevelt addresses Washington's German societies, and he wires Alice forbidding her to pour tea at a charity show.

events.detail: Quentin's 6th birthday party in the nursery
Receives and addresses the German societies of Washington
Letter to Kermit; telegram to Alice

letters.topic: Aunt Emily's arrival; Quentin's birthday
Telegram: she must not sell tea at a charity show

headline: Alice pours tea anyway
summary: Roosevelt meets the Cabinet and at 2:30 the Panama commission with Bunau-Varilla. In New York, Alice ignores his wishes and serves tea at $5 a cup at the Charity Portrait Show with Ethel Barrymore and Maude Adams.

events.detail: With Bunau-Varilla and the Panama commission
Alice pours tea at a New York charity show against his objections

headline: Caruso's Met debut
summary: Roosevelt lunches with W. D. Murphy, goes over the Bristow report with Payne and Bristow, sees Tawney and, at 2:30, the Russian ambassador, and dines with Joe Bishop. In New York, Enrico Caruso makes his Metropolitan Opera debut in Rigoletto.

events.detail: Postal report reviewed with Bristow and Payne
Caruso sings in Rigoletto at the Metropolitan Opera

uncertain: The record does not name the Russian ambassador; he is identified as Count Cassini.

headline: Sunday with nothing recorded
summary: Roosevelt is in Washington; no activity is noted.

headline: Opening the German-American fair by button
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Senator Platt and G. W. Dunn, sees Foraker and Fairbanks, and at seven touches an electric button that starts the German-American fair at Convention Hall before meeting Hanna at 8:30. He writes Philip Stewart about Colorado politics and bear hunting.

events.detail: Opens the German-American fair by pressing a button
Writes Philip Stewart about bears and Colorado politics

letters.topic: Colorado politics; hunting bears

headline: Peacemaking between Platt and Odell
summary: After the Cabinet takes up Panama, Roosevelt brings Governor Odell, Senator Platt and Dunn together to settle their New York feud. He lunches with Montana labor leaders, Cortelyou, MacVeagh and Carroll Wright, meets the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and keeps Odell overnight.

events.detail: Tries to reconcile the Platt and Odell factions
Lunch with Montana union men, Cortelyou, MacVeagh and Wright

uncertain: A name is unclear in the record; it is read as Odell.

headline: Bamie's anniversary, a full calendar
summary: Bamie marks eight years of marriage. On a packed day Roosevelt lunches with Slicer and Shaw and meets Austria's ambassador.
uncertain: 'Shaw' assumed to be Leslie M. Shaw.

headline: Thanksgiving, then north for Uncle Jimmie
summary: On Thanksgiving evening Roosevelt leaves for New York after the death of his uncle James K. Gracie and stays at Corinne's, where Eleanor is also a guest; everyone but Eleanor goes out to play. He answers Packard's charge that he is anti-labor and tells G. H. Putnam of a Collier's deal for his collected works.

events.detail: Uncle James K. Gracie has died
Evening trip to New York City; stays with Corinne
Niece Eleanor also at Corinne's; the others go out to play
Letters to Packard and G. H. Putnam

letters.topic: Rebuts the claim that he opposes organized labor
Collier's arrangement for his collected works

headline: Uncle Jimmie Gracie's funeral
summary: Roosevelt attends the funeral of his uncle James K. Gracie in New York and returns to Washington.

headline: A crank at the funeral
summary: Roosevelt sees S. Fred Nixon at ten, meets Ball, Quay and Fairbanks, and lunches with Eugene Philbin. He tells Kermit that 500 police ringed the church at Uncle Jimmie's funeral, yet a crank slipped in with a petition about curing the Kaiser's cancer. Ted has sprained an ankle and is urged to read Trevelyan's American Revolution.

events.detail: Letters to Kermit, Ted, John Biddle, Ralph Trautmann and Butler

letters.topic: The funeral, the police and a crank
His sprained ankle; read Trevelyan
Against paving Rock Creek Park's paths
Ellis Island

headline: His Bristow report comments go public
summary: Roosevelt's comments on the Bristow report on postal frauds are published.

events.detail: Publication of his remarks on the Bristow postal report

headline: Was Panama like the Confederacy?
summary: Roosevelt receives Cannon with an Illinois delegation and dines with Senators Spooner and Orville Platt. To Otto Gresham he explains why Panama's break from Colombia is no parallel to Southern secession: the Panamanians have right on their side.

events.detail: Dinner with Spooner and O. H. Platt
To Otto Gresham on Panama and the Civil War comparison

letters.topic: Why Panama is not like the South in 1861

headline: Lunch with Captain Pershing
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt lunches with Captain John J. Pershing, Monsignor O'Connell and Major and Mrs. Howze, confers with Senator Penrose, and writes Joe Bishop about press guesswork over his talk with Platt and Odell.

events.detail: Lunch with Pershing, O'Connell and the Howzes
To Joe Bishop on the Platt-Odell meeting and newspaper speculation

letters.topic: Press rumors about his Platt-Odell talks

headline: Panama ratifies the canal treaty
summary: As he and Edith mark 17 years of marriage, Panama's government ratifies the Hay-Bunau-Varilla treaty. Roosevelt talks Panama and Illinois with Cullom, lunches with John R. Proctor and Garfield, sees Foraker, Fairbanks and the British ambassador, and writes Arthur von Briesen on immigration tests.

Lunch with John R. Proctor and Garfield

headline: Alaska result "satisfactory in every way"
summary: Roosevelt confers with Root, Moody and Hay, lunches with Ray Stannard Baker, and sends Congress a message on the Alaska boundary award.

events.detail: Meetings with Secretaries Hay, Moody and Root
Sends Congress a message on the Alaska award

headline: Hanna at night on canal and Wood
summary: Roosevelt sees Hill of the Tribune at ten, meets the Cabinet, takes up New York appointments with Senator Platt and confers with Hay. At 9:15 p.m. he and Hanna go over canal legislation, the Wood case and the national committee chairmanship.

events.detail: Platt on New York patronage; Hay
Hanna on the canal bill, Wood and the party chairmanship

headline: Breakfast with Putnam
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts with Putnam and writes Hanna about rumors swirling around his meeting with Platt and Odell.

summary: Roosevelt confers in the evening with Joseph Bristow and Francis Leupp.

events.detail: Evening talk with Bristow and Leupp

headline: Annual message: building the canal is a duty
summary: Congress opens its regular session and hears Roosevelt's annual message, which calls building the Panama canal a national duty. He confers with Senator Warren on Alaska and lunches with Gordon and Peck. To Arthur Lee he praises the Alaska settlement and teases that Britain did well to face such reasonable jurors.

To Arthur Lee on the Alaska award

headline: Langley's machine fails again
summary: Charles Manly makes a second try at flying Professor Langley's aircraft off the Potomac, and fails again. Roosevelt meets the Cabinet, lunches with Andrew Carnegie, Henry Pritchett, Moody and others, and dines at Root's at eight.

events.detail: Second failed launch of Langley's aerodrome
Lunch with Carnegie, Pritchett, Moody and others

headline: Panama tops his worries
summary: Roosevelt confers with Representative Foss on the Navy, visits Root in the evening and sees Senator Aldrich at 8:30. He tells Charles Osborn that Panama concerns him more than anything else right now.

letters.topic: Panama is his chief worry

headline: Commander Winslow joins as aide

Letters to Trevelyan, Abbott, Root and Polk

headline: Riis at the White House
summary: Roosevelt talks statehood with Delegate Wilson, sees Root, Moody, Proctor, Cockrell and Foraker, and meets Shaw and von Sternberg about exports to Germany. Jacob Riis is his guest. He writes Austin Wadsworth about New York business jitters over his financial course.

headline: Funeral for a civil service commissioner
summary: At 10:30 Roosevelt attends the funeral of Civil Service Commissioner John R. Proctor, then lunches with Shaw and Speaker Cannon and discusses German export duties. Beveridge calls at nine and Riis stays over. He names John Black to Proctor's seat.

headline: Senate passes Cuban reciprocity

events.detail: Lunch with Lodge, Crane, Root, Cortelyou, Kennedy and Jones

letters.topic: Support for Peary's North Pole expedition

summary: Roosevelt calls in Knox, Lodge, Root, Moody, Hitchcock and Cortelyou to deal with land frauds in the West, lunches with Judge Grosscup, and dines with Joe Bishop, Professor Lounsbury and Nicholas Murray Butler, who stays over. headline: On the rights of citizenship
summary: Roosevelt meets the Spanish minister and Root, attends Miss Locke's funeral at St. Paul's at two, and visits Bamie that evening. In short, I wanted to add my mite toward the effort to persuade the southerners simply to treat negroes as they would other people.

headline: Stockings on the President's bed
summary: At seven on Christmas morning the children pile onto Roosevelt's bed to open their stockings, while Allan, Kermit's terrier, sits in the thick of it and Bob Ferguson and Aunt Emily looking on. headline: Henry Adams frowns at the court
summary: Roosevelt confers with Quay and sees Allison, Hopkins, Boutell and Mondell. At the evening diplomatic reception Henry Adams is struck by what he considers royal trappings and imperial airs, and judges the presidency changed for the worse. Roosevelt writes Douglas Robinson on family money and Burlingame a comic verse about Panama.

Evening reception for the diplomatic corps
Letters to Douglas Robinson, Root, Hitchcock and Burlingame

Cherokee lands
A funny poem about Panama

headline: Senators all day, music at night
summary: Roosevelt confers with Representative Hinshaw and Senators Foraker, Aldrich, Fairbanks and Orville Platt, then with John Sleicher and Maurice Low, before a White House dinner and a ten o'clock musicale.

headline: "I ought to be dead"
summary: Roosevelt meets Arthur von Briesen's Ellis Island commission at nine, confers with Congressmen Bartholdt and Burton, Senators Allison and Dolliver, and at 2:30 Ambassador von Sternberg. He tells Jacob Riis his biography is so kind it embarrasses him.

events.detail: Ellis Island commission with von Briesen
With Burton and Bartholdt; then Dolliver and Allison
Callers McCleary, Alger, Mitchell and Quay
To Jacob Riis about his biography

letters.topic: Embarrassed by Riis's flattering biography

tr_quotes.text: I feel ashamed on reading your biography of me, for I feel as though I ought to be dead in order to justify it!

headline: Two Scotts at 9:30
summary: Two evening callers, Captain Charles H. Scott and John Winfield Scott, see the President.

events.detail: Evening visit from Captain Charles Scott and John Winfield Scott

headline: Steering Ted away from West Point
summary: Roosevelt is photographed at nine, confers with Kearns and Aldrich, sees Governor Durbin and others, and lunches with Root, Knox, Beveridge and MacVeagh. He writes Ted weighing military against civilian careers and hoping he will skip West Point and Annapolis.

events.detail: Durbin, Fulton, Landis and Mitchell call
Lunch with Knox, MacVeagh, Beveridge and Root

letters.topic: Military versus civilian life; would rather he avoid the academies

headline: Persian minister and a Knox dinner
summary: After the Cabinet, Roosevelt meets Senator Elkins, sees Representative Champ Clark, receives Ambassador von Sternberg at 12:30 and the Persian minister at 2:30, and dines with Edith at the Knoxes'.

headline: Naval Academy appointments
summary: Roosevelt confers with Lucius Littauer and sees Penrose, Governor Murray Crane, and Moody, who comes to review Naval Academy appointments.

events.detail: Goes over Naval Academy appointments with Moody

headline: Snowy ride; Hanna told who the nominee is
summary: After a day of callers, the Roosevelts take their horses through deep snow along Rock Creek, and the White House holds its diplomatic dinner at eight. He writes Hanna, after press talk of a Hanna candidacy, leaving no doubt that he himself will be the nominee.

events.detail: Ride with Edith up snowy Rock Creek

letters.topic: Makes plain that he, not Hanna, will be the candidate

headline: Ida Tarbell calls
summary: Roosevelt meets the Cabinet, talks New York politics with Woodruff and confers with Beveridge, sees Senator Long at ten and Sternberg at 12:30, lunches with Norman and Alderman, and receives Ida Tarbell at three. He and Edith ride again through the snow before a 10 p.m. musicale.

events.detail: Woodruff on New York politics; Beveridge
To William Sulzer on the Considine case

letters.topic: Review of James Considine's five-year sentence for mail robbery

headline: Callers and canal talks
summary: Among a crowd of callers are Quay, Governor Hill and Senator Beveridge. Roosevelt confers with Hay and Representative Hitt.

events.detail: Callers include Hill, Beveridge and Quay

headline: Writing Morley about Gladstone
summary: Roosevelt writes John Morley about his life of Gladstone; Morley plans to visit Washington in December.

events.detail: To John Morley on his Gladstone biography

letters.topic: His Gladstone book; a planned December visit

headline: Michigan Republicans and a juggler
summary: On Bamie's 49th birthday Roosevelt receives a Michigan Republican delegation led by Senators Alger and Burrows, sees Rockhill and Amos Pinchot among others, and sits for Hewitt at 2:30. He tells Kermit the family went to see Kellar the magician, and Ted that he relaxes with riding and broadsword bouts.

events.detail: Michigan Republicans led by Alger and Burrows
Callers Rockhill, Amos Pinchot, Tawney, Crumpacker and Grosvenor
Letters to Kermit, Crane, Spring-Rice and Ted

letters.topic: Family outing to see Kellar's show
Will meet New York businessmen
Russia, Persia and Panama
Riding and broadsword for exercise

uncertain: The record says Kellar juggled; Harry Kellar was a stage magician.

headline: Hanna won't fight, he thinks
summary: Hewitt photographs the President at nine and Edith at 2:30. The Cabinet takes up the canal treaty, and Roosevelt confers with Senators Cullom and Allison about it. He and Edith dine at the Paynes', and he tells Joe Bishop he doubts Hanna will contest the nomination.

events.detail: Allison and Cullom on the treaty
Callers Cummins, Lodge, Platt, Hemenway, Bartholdt and others

letters.topic: Expects no nomination fight from Hanna

uncertain: The record lists a 'Governor Doliver' among callers, which is unclear. 'Platt' may be either senator of that name.

headline: Springy is engaged
summary: Hewitt photographs the President again at nine. Roosevelt confers with Aldrich on the canal treaty while the House debates the Hepburn pure food bill. Spring-Rice writes Edith from St. Petersburg that he is to marry Florence Lascelles, whom he has known eight years.

events.detail: Smoot, Proctor and O. H. Platt call
House takes up the Hepburn pure food bill
Spring-Rice announces his engagement to Edith; Roosevelt writes Spooner on the treaty

letters.topic: To Edith: his engagement to Florence Lascelles
The Panama treaty

headline: Jusserand and the judicial reception
summary: Senators Cullom, Frye and Hopkins and the Board of Indian Commissioners call. Roosevelt receives French Ambassador Jusserand at 2:30 and hosts the judicial reception that evening.

events.detail: Callers Frye, Hopkins, Cullom and the Indian commissioners
Letter to Ambassador Powell Clayton in Mexico

letters.topic: Not described

headline: Miles likened to Wilkinson
summary: After the Cabinet, Roosevelt discusses Ohio with Foraker, sees former Governor Merriam and Millard, lunches with Knox and Gates, and hosts a 10 p.m. musicale. Japanese troops land in Korea. He praises Alfred Henry Lewis's The Boss and tells George Harvey that General Miles resembles the early republic's James Wilkinson.

events.detail: Letters to Lewis, Joe Bishop and George Harvey

letters.topic: Enjoyed his novel The Boss
A fiscal agency in Panama
Wood and Miles; Miles compared to James Wilkinson

headline: Boone and Crockett dinner
summary: Roosevelt talks canal treaty with Fairbanks, sees Cannon, Grosvenor, Chief Justice Fuller and Justice Harlan, confers with Root, and lunches with Caspar Whitney and Lodge. At eight he goes to the Metropolitan Club to dine with his fellow Boone and Crockett members. He tells Kermit that Ethel is wonderful with the little boys and reports on Loretta the parrot.

events.detail: Fairbanks on the canal treaty; Root
Fuller, Harlan, Cannon and Grosvenor call
Lunch with Caspar Whitney and Lodge
Letters to Payne, Kermit and Grenville Dodge

Ethel and the boys; Loretta the parrot
New York City's Republican committee

tr_quotes.text: Ethel is as good as gold with both the little boys.

headline: A blank Sunday
summary: Roosevelt is in Washington; no activity is recorded.

headline: On writing history
summary: Roosevelt confers with Heyburn, Shaw and Beveridge and sees Dalzell and Lodge. He writes Trevelyan about the craft of history and asks Cortelyou to let Quan Yick Nam, a merchant from China, enter the country.

letters.topic: How history should be written
Admit Chinese merchant Quan Yick Nam

references.pages: end of Vol. III; start of Vol. IV

headline: Good roads from St. Louis
summary: After a Cabinet session on Panama, Roosevelt meets St. Louis's good roads committee, sees Delaware's two senators and Representative Smith, and dines at Moody's. He sends Cullom State Department papers on Panama and Root and Moody memos on Wood and on Army and Navy actions on the isthmus.

events.detail: Letters to Cullom, Root and Moody

letters.topic: State Department Panama correspondence
Memo on General Wood; Army actions in Panama
Navy actions in Panama

headline: Honoring Root at Alger's
summary: Heyburn, George Perkins and Metcalf call, and Sternberg comes at 2:30. From nine to midnight Roosevelt attends a reception for Elihu Root at Russell Alger's home. He tells Hay he opposes the Philippine inter-island shipping bills.

events.detail: Callers Heyburn, Metcalf and Senator Perkins
Reception for Root at Alger's house
To Hay on the Philippine shipping bills

letters.topic: Why he is against the Philippine shipping bills in the Senate

headline: Supreme Court dinner
summary: Roosevelt talks Nebraska politics with Millard, lunches with Root, Taft and Bonaparte, confers with Chauncey Depew, sees the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission, and at eight gives the Supreme Court dinner.

events.detail: Lunch with Taft, Bonaparte and Root

headline: "I doubt if they can prevent my nomination"
summary: After the Cabinet and callers including Aldrich and Beveridge, Roosevelt lunches with Governor Crane, joins a reception for William Howard Taft, and closes with a White House dinner and musicale. He tells Ted that Hanna and Wall Street worry him a little but cannot likely stop him.

events.detail: Cabinet meeting; callers include Landis, Hemenway, Ball, Beveridge and Aldrich
To Ted on his nomination prospects

letters.topic: Hanna and Wall Street; his chances of election

tr_quotes.text: Senator Hanna and the Wall Street crowd are causing me some worry but not of a serious: kind. I doubt if they can prevent my nomination.

uncertain: The quote keeps a stray colon after 'serious' as the record gives it.

headline: Gridiron dinner; nomination "assured"
summary: Roosevelt confers with Crane and Kohlsaat and on Ohio with Foraker, lunches with Alice French, Mrs. Oliver Wendell Holmes, Pinchot and Taft, and goes to the Gridiron Club's dinner; Butler is his overnight guest. He thanks Albert Shaw for friendly editorials and says his nomination is now certain.

events.detail: Callers Cullom, Shaw, Littauer, Proctor, Hemenway and Goodrich
Lunch with Alice French, Mrs. Holmes, Pinchot and Taft

letters.topic: Thanks for supportive editorials; nomination now sure

headline: Root, Taft, Moody and Archbishop Ireland
summary: After a dinner for Elihu Root, Roosevelt sees Governor Taft at nine, Secretary Moody at 9:30 and Archbishop Ireland at ten. Critics are attacking the Roosevelts' style of living and what they call an imperial presidency.

events.detail: Taft, then Moody, then Archbishop Ireland
Criticism of the Roosevelts' lifestyle and an 'imperial' presidency
